extraction.name: ChartQA
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark for question answering about charts with visual and logical reasoning, containing human-written and machine-generated question-answer pairs over real-world charts.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four online sources (Statista, Pew Research, Our World in Data, OECD). For Pew, only chart images were crawled; for the other three, underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and text descriptions were extracted. Human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk, and additional QA pairs were generated automatically from human-written Statista summaries using T5 and filtered heuristically.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For the Pew dataset, underlying data tables were unavailable, so only chart images were collected.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include chart images from Statista, Pew Research, Our World in Data, and OECD; additionally, underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and associated text descriptions were collected when available.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was augmented by generating QA pairs from human-written chart summaries using two fine-tuned T5 models for answer extraction and answer-aware question generation. Invalid generated questions were filtered out using a heuristic based on whether the answer could be found in the chart data table, and the machine-generated test set was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For non-Pew sources, underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and text descriptions were extracted. Bounding box information for chart elements was extracted from SVG files to train data extraction models. Generated QA pairs were filtered heuristically to remove incomplete or unanswerable questions, and datasets were randomly split into train, validation, and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-authored QA pairs were collected on Amazon Mechanical Turk. Workers were asked to write two questions per chart focusing on compositional and visual questions, and provide answers. The same questions were then answered by another annotator; if answers matched exactly, the answer was accepted, otherwise the authors manually checked and selected the final correct answer. Additional QA pairs were machine-generated from human-written Statista summaries using T5 models for answer extraction and answer-aware question generation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between crowdworkers based on exact matches was 61.04%. Manual checking of 500 random samples found agreement increased to 78.55% when typos and lexical variations were considered. For machine-generated QA pairs, 1,250 pairs were manually analyzed and 86.64% were found complete, answerable, and correct.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk crowdworkers in the United States
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Chart topics may include social and economic issues, demographic trends, public opinion, politics, economy, health, and society; annotator data were anonymized.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors note that the models could be abused to mislead the public about chart content and implications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The Pew subset is heavily skewed toward U.S. Politics & Policy, and bar charts are the most common chart type across the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Machine-generated questions can be incomplete or unanswerable due to domain mismatch. Model performance drops when gold data tables are unavailable because automatic chart data extraction remains challenging. The models struggle with nested logical operations, complex visual compositional questions, and certain chart types such as pie charts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for training, validation, and testing chart question answering systems, especially for visual and logical reasoning over charts.
